# Temporary SingleFile font serialization fix

The source excerpt and patch in this directory are derived from
[single-file-core](https://github.com/gildas-lormeau/single-file-core), commit
`79ecf4dce4acab130c0b587d8843f0328eb389f9`,
[`core/lib/processor-helper-common.js`](https://github.com/gildas-lormeau/single-file-core/blob/79ecf4dce4acab130c0b587d8843f0328eb389f9/core/lib/processor-helper-common.js).

Modified 2026-11-07: reuse the CSS value already generated by `getPropertyValue`
instead of serializing the selected value twice; use nested exact-string Maps
for scope/descriptor and source keys rather than concatenating full font data
into duplicate-rule keys; cache repeated source parsing for one pass. String
coercion and source equality are preserved.
The readable changes are in
`font-serialization.patch`; the preparation hook carries the exact original
and modified minified methods plus original/patched bundle hashes. No font
selection or capture options change.

This copied/modified upstream material remains licensed under GNU AGPL version
3 or, at your option, any later version, not the surrounding repository's MIT
license. The full upstream license is reproduced in `AGPL-3.0.txt`. The
additional permission below applies only to unmodified files, not this patch.
The preparation copies the whole installed extension, retaining its notices;
it does not edit the shared provider installation.

Remove the temporary preparation and these patch materials after an upstream
release includes this fix and the full-fidelity gallery regression passes.

## Temporary compatibility restriction

The preparation hook and `singlefile_extension_save.js` capture guard require
reviewed SingleFile 1.36.0 and the exact prepared bundle hash. Unprepared,
changed, or future unreviewed versions fail SingleFile clearly before capture;
other plugins and Chrome startup retain their existing behavior. Remove both
the preparation hook and this guard when adopting a validated upstream fix.

The third change caches source splitting and parsed font metadata by exact string
equality for one font-processing pass, including nested scopes and stylesheets.
Each rule receives a fresh array and metadata record; validity mutations remain
independent. Regular expressions, fallback order, source selection, and embedded
font bytes are unchanged. These caches are released at the end of the pass.

The corresponding-source diff uses zero-context unified hunks to preserve
upstream tab indentation without whitespace-tool ambiguity. Apply it to the
exact upstream commit with `git apply --unidiff-zero font-serialization.patch`.

## Temporary stage2 diagnostic overlay (not a production fix)

The workflow's separate diagnostic81 hook starts from the unchanged pure
candidate hash and applies the explicit `core_changes` before/after source
pairs. Its distinct final hash is accepted only by the temporary workflow's
capture guard and verifier. The plugin's production guard remains unchanged.
These modified excerpts are also AGPL-3.0-or-later under the original notice
above. Corresponding source is the auditable `core_changes` list in
`../../workflows/diagnose-canva.yml`, based on the same core commit's
`core/index.js`, `core/lib/processor-helper-common.js`, and
`core/lib/processor-helper-inline.js`. Original bundled notices remain intact.
Remove this overlay with the diagnostic workflow; do not ship it in the plugin.

The fixed phase schema remains `{phase, a, b, elapsed_ms}`. `stage_start` and
`stage_end` use `a` for step0–5 and `b` for the child-frame boolean. They never
include frame identifiers, URLs, options or content. `detail` uses `a` for the
following fixed counter and `b` for its numeric value:

- 0/1: synchronous stage2 task entry/exit (three tasks in source order).
- 2/3 and4/5: root and child font-alternative branch entry/exit.
- 6/7: font metadata traversal entry/exit.
- 8/9: source metadata parsing entry/exit.
- 10/11: repeated-rule marking entry/exit.
- 12/13 and14/15: root and child frame branch entry/exit.
- 16/17: child runner run entry/exit.
- 18/19: child getPageData serialization entry/exit.
- 20/21: child embedding entry/exit.
- 22: completed font validation cache hit.
- 23/24: primary FontFace constructor entry/exit.
- 25: primary existing load timer fired.
- 26: fallback FontFace constructor entry.
- 27: fallback existing load timer fired.
- 28: uncached source validation completed (including non-FontFace sources).
- 29/30: retained CSS source reparsing entry/success.
- 31: outstanding primary validation count, including fallback work.

Counters are local to the content realm and aggregate root/child work except
where explicitly distinguished. First16 counts and subsequent powers of two
are emitted, then all counters are flushed at a completed font branch. The
outstanding gauge emits at0/1 and powers of two. Thus a timed-out run's latest
counter can be a lower bound, not the exact final total. Gauge snapshots can
also be stale between checkpoints. No new await, promise handler, timer,
network request, option or deadline is introduced. Observation has finite
CPU/console overhead and is not a timing-neutral benchmark.

The collector retains at most one latest entry per detail code (32 total),
within the existing512-record cap. Codes outside0–31, noninteger values,
negative counts, counts over1048576 and nonboolean stage frame values are
rejected. Only the existing three JSON filenames are upload-eligible.
GC tracing is unchanged: CDP delivers collected events after tracing ends;
an externally terminated helper can legitimately leave no GC JSON.


## Branch-only native font-validation measurement

This additional overlay is restricted to manual execution on
`diagnostics/canva-font-validation-rc78`, based on held rc78. It does not change
production candidate code, release workflows, capture options or deadlines.
Its complete corresponding-source before/after pairs remain in the diagnostic
workflow under the same AGPL-3.0-or-later notice and full license above.

The additional `metric` phase uses fixed integer codes0–44 and numeric values
only. Timing values are integer microseconds measured with `performance.now()`.
For each pair below the first code is cumulative duration and the second is
maximum duration:

- 0: uncached source entries;1: unique exact-src misses within each existing
  fontTests cache;2: same-src misses overlapping another active miss.
- 3: maximum active misses in any one cache;4: completed-cache hits.
- 5: primary FontFace constructor starts;6/7: constructor duration.
- 8: primary existing load calls;9/10: synchronous load-call duration.
- 11/12: primary await resolved by load/timer;13/14: NetworkError/other rejection;
  15/16: settled primary await duration, excluding fallback work.
- 17: original-resource fallback scans;18/19: scan duration.
- 20: fallback constructor starts;21/22: constructor duration.
- 23: existing fallback load calls;24/25: synchronous call duration.
- 26/27/28: fallback await resolved by load/timer/rejected;29/30: settled duration.
- 31: retained-source joins;32/33: join duration.
- 34: retained CSS parses;35/36: successful parse duration;37: join/parse exception.
- 38/39: primary/fallback timer firings, including late loser timers.
- 40/41: completed-cache lookup duration;42: reserved and never emitted.
- 43: validation entry count;44: current unfinished uncached validations.

Exact source comparison uses the source records already retained by pending
validation. A WeakMap keyed by the existing fontTests map holds an active-record
array; records are removed at the original cache write. It creates no source
copies, payload digests or persistent set of font strings. Strings and source
records are never logged. Counts are per existing cache, then aggregated across
root/child caches, not global payload identity. Exact-string comparisons add
observation cost; this is not a timing-neutral benchmark.

No new promises, handlers, awaits, timers or load calls are added. Measurements
surround the existing constructor, load call, race settlement, fallback scan,
join and parse. Outcome bookkeeping does not change source validity or cancel
existing timers. A constructor that throws or an unfinished await contributes
no completed duration; code37 includes join/parse exceptions without a duration.
Concurrent await-duration sums can exceed wall time and must not be treated as
CPU time. Existing sparse emission means unfinished-run totals and maxima are
lower bounds and the pending gauge may be stale. Completed font branches flush
all recorded aggregates. The collector keeps at most45 latest metric entries
alongside32 detail entries within the512-record cap, rejecting values outside
0–1000000000000 and codes outside0–44. No additional artifact is uploaded.
